extracted.intended_audience: researchers and advanced students in linguistics/pragmatics and humour studies; theoreticians and analysts of jokes (also useful to humorists interested in cognitive/pragmatic strategies)
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and classification of jokes according to sources of incongruity (frame-based vs discourse-centered), location (setup vs punchline), and type of resolution (discourse-centered, frame-based, implication-based); includes a twelve-Case taxonomy and descriptions of inferential sub-strategies. Useful for analysing or designing jokes from a relevance-theoretic stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incongruity-resolution pattern (IR model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most jokes follow a dual-phase (set-up → detection of incongruity → resolution) pattern: the hearer encounters an incongruity during processing and must find a resolution to obtain the intended humorous effects (Suls; relevance-theoretic framing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat jokes as sequences where an initial interpretation becomes inconsistent and the hearer must either resolve the inconsistency (typical) or entertain clashing interpretations (e.g., some puns, nonsense humour). Examples: punchlines that force reinterpretation or backtracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish frame-based vs discourse-centered incongruity
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame-based incongruity arises from errors or alternatives in the make-sense frame (the mental scenario/schema) constructed for the joke; discourse-centered incongruity arises from inferential operations on the text (reference assignment, disambiguation, concept adjustment, saturation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify source of incongruity by whether it lies in the constructed scenario (frame) or in the inferential enrichment of the verbal material; many jokes combine both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location of source: setup vs punchline
rubrics_metrics.description: The taxonomy distinguishes whether the source of the incongruity is located in the setup or in the punchline; this affects processing (e.g., backtracking required when source is in setup).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When coding jokes, mark whether the element enabling incongruity appears early (setup) or at the end (punchline); note that identification and source can be in different positions (e.g., an underdetermined phrase in the setup later reinterpreted by the punchline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourse-centered resolution (resolution type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution requiring supplementary inferential operations on the text (selecting an undetected sense, choosing a different referent, adjusting an ad hoc concept) to obtain the explicature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for operations such as disambiguation, reference reassignment, saturation or concept adjustment being used to reconcile text-level inconsistencies; applies only to operations aimed at explicature (explicit interpretation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame-based resolution (resolution type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution that requires altering or replacing the make-sense frame constructed for the joke so that the whole joke becomes coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify when the hearer must adopt a new scenario/frame (often global to the joke) rather than performing local textual inferencing; many classical one-liners rely on frame replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implication-based resolution (resolution type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution achieved by deriving implicatures beyond the explicature; these implicated premises/conclusions rely on contextual information and are not directly tied to the explicit interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect when humour comes from a set of implicated conclusions (strong or weak) inferred after the explicature; often used to generate additional humorous assumptions (e.g., stereotype-based implicatures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case 1: [frame-based incongruity] [setup] [discourse-centered resolution]
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearer builds a make-sense frame in the setup that becomes incongruous with subsequent material; resolution requires discourse-centered inferencing. (Author notes such cases are difficult to find; no samples in corpus.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rare/infrequent; expect theoretical rather than empirical instances. Antipattern: assuming frequent occurrence without corpus evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case 2: [frame-based incongruity] [punchline] [discourse-centered resolution]
rubrics_metrics.description: A make-sense frame is built until the punchline invalidates it; resolution demands reinterpretation of some part of the joke via discourse inferencing. (No samples found in the corpus; example provided in prior research.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for punchlines that force reinterpretation via textual inferencing rather than full frame replacement; flagged as scarce in sample data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case 3: [frame-based incongruity] [setup] [frame-based resolution]
rubrics_metrics.description: Incongruity discovered during construction of the make-sense frame in the setup; resolution requires substituting or altering the frame (frame replacement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common pattern: multiple possible frames for the setup, one selected but later replaced; examples: stories where an initially assumed motive/scene is later reinterpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case 4: [frame-based incongruity] [punchline] [frame-based resolution]
rubrics_metrics.description: Make-sense frame constructed unobstructed until the punchline invalidates it; resolution requires changing the frame for the whole joke (global frame replacement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very frequent in classic joke topics (e.g., marriage jokes); the punchline triggers a wholesale frame shift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case 5: [frame-based incongruity] [setup] [implication-based resolution]
rubrics_metrics.description: Setup induces a frame-based incongruity whose resolution is mainly achieved by deriving implicated premises and conclusions beyond the explicature (implicatures). (Uncommon.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect implicature-heavy resolutions where the hearer constructs implied attitudes/assumptions to reconcile frame-based anomalies (e.g., purchase-of-mule joke).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case 6: [frame-based incongruity] [punchline] [implication-based resolution]
rubrics_metrics.description: Punchline produces a frame-based incongruity and its resolution depends on the derivation of multiple implicatures; frequent in corpus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punchlines that suddenly make a host of assumptions accessible, producing humour through a cluster of implicated conclusions (e.g., adultery/lovers examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case 7: [discourse-centered incongruity] [setup] [discourse-centered resolution]
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical garden-path structure: the setup contains covert ambiguity with one meaning effortlessly accessible; the punchline invalidates that earlier inference, forcing backtracking and reprocessing of the initial part to appreciate the alternative meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for classic garden-path jokes where early text is reinterpreted (e.g., puns that rely on undetected senses becoming salient only after the punchline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case 8: [discourse-centered incongruity] [punchline] [discourse-centered resolution]
rubrics_metrics.description: Discourse-centered incongruity whose source is in the punchline; resolution requires text-level inferential operations to reach explicature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punchlines that enable a different interpretation of earlier discourse elements via disambiguation, reference reassignment, or other inferential operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case 9: [discourse-centered incongruity] [setup] [frame-based resolution]
rubrics_metrics.description: Discourse-based incongruity originates in the setup (text/inferential ambiguity) but its resolution requires changing the make-sense frame (frame replacement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for setups that invite a particular textual interpretation which later forces adopting a new scenario to reconcile meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case 10: [discourse-centered incongruity] [punchline] [frame-based resolution]
rubrics_metrics.description: Discourse-based incongruity located in the punchline whose resolution entails frame alteration for the whole joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punchlines that reassign textual meaning and thereby mandate a new global scenario (e.g., reinterpretation of previously encoded events).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case 11: [discourse-centered incongruity] [setup] [implication-based resolution]
rubrics_metrics.description: Source of discourse-centered incongruity in the setup, resolved primarily by deriving implicatures beyond the explicature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect the hearer to infer attitudes/premises from the setup's textual ambiguity rather than simply altering frames or explicatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case 12: [discourse-centered incongruity] [punchline] [implication-based resolution]
rubrics_metrics.description: Discourse-centered incongruity located in the punchline whose resolution depends on implicature derivation; data show this Case occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punchlines that trigger many implicated conclusions (strong and weak) which together produce humour; common in jokes that exploit background cultural knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourse-centered sub-strategy: disambiguation
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearer chooses between senses of the same word to match speaker intent (e.g., bank = river bank/financial institution); disambiguation is used as a resolution move.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classic mechanism in puns and lexical ambiguity jokes; speakers anticipate the likely accessible sense and later exploit the alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourse-centered sub-strategy: concept adjustment (ad hoc concepts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pragmatic adjustment of the prototypical concept associated with a word to a contextually modified (narrower or broader) ad hoc concept (e.g., DRINK* vs DRINK).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for jokes that exploit shifting category membership or prototypical features; identify when concept narrowing/broadening explains the punchline's fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourse-centered sub-strategy: saturation (gap-filling/unarticulated constituents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearer fills elided or unarticulated parts of an utterance necessary for interpretation (e.g., comparisons like 'better [than what?]').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for sub-sentential signs or brackets implied by context; saturation often underlies implicature-rich humour and some frame shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourse-centered sub-strategy: reference assignment (indexicals/proper names)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment of referents to empty indexicals or names; jokes exploit alternate referents accessible in context (e.g., 'it' or numerals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common sub-strategy in the corpus (third most frequent); test pronouns/indexicals for multiple plausible referents that a punchline can foreground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourse-centered sub-strategy: retrieval of unarticulated constituents & alternative constituent arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recovering missing constituents (typical in signs/short utterances) and exploiting alternative syntactic/logical forms (e.g., outstanding/in their field vs out standing in their field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mechanisms produce structural ambiguity used for comedic reinterpretation; check for sentences that admit distinct logical form groupings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garden-path / backtracking mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: The speaker creates a covert ambiguity in the first part so one meaning is effortlessly accessible; the second part invalidates that inference and prompts backtracking and reprocessing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label jokes using this mechanism as garden-path; expect a distinct perceptual surprise and a reanalysis effort that often yields humour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why incongruity is pleasurable (sources of humorous enjoyment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Four proposed contributing factors: (a) shared expectation of humorous context that licenses norm violations; (b) pleasure in solving incongruities (discovery/triump); (c) realization of having been fooled (benign deception); (d) positive interaction with addressee's beliefs and accessible information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these dimensions to assess why a resolved incongruity elicits amusement; they also suggest how context/speaker addressee relations modulate funniness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of discrepancy / complexity effect on funniness
rubrics_metrics.description: The magnitude of discrepancy between expected interpretation and forced interpretation influences enjoyment: some research suggests moderate discrepancies maximize humour (easier resolution → reward), while others claim larger discrepancies increase funniness; very complex resolutions may reduce humour because of processing difficulty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating jokes, consider processing effort vs reward; watch for cross-study disagreement and account for cultural/topic differences and audience processing capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stereotype-consistent information as an anti-pattern for IR
rubrics_metrics.description: When joke content matches the hearer's preexisting stereotypical beliefs, no incongruity may be perceived (no IR pattern); humour relying on stereotypes often depends on implicatures rather than IR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious: stereotype reinforcement may produce humour via implicated conclusions rather than an explicit incongruity; also ethical considerations and cultural variation mean such jokes may not produce the same effects across audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed/ambiguous case ascription (multiple strategies or blurred boundaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some jokes do not fit neatly into a single Case because (a) frame vs discourse distinction is blurred, (b) multiple frames are constructed/invalidated, (c) the source of incongruity is distributed or (d) multiple discourse sub-strategies are engaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow multi-labeling or note problematic ascriptions; expect roughly 10/500 corpus jokes to be difficult to ascribe cleanly. When analyzing, record all operative sub-strategies and frame shifts.
